page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The deal is off!
title: The deal is off!
description:
Paul, the boss, is sending Anna and Tom on a business trip to France. He wants them to clinch the deal with a company which is interested in buying their Imperial Lemons. But has Tom got more than business on his mind?
This episode focuses on what to say when you need to book a flight.
phrases: What is the outbound and return date?
Do you want to fly business or economy?
Do you want a fixed or flexible ticket?
Would you like a window or aisle seat?
Have you got a frequent flyer number?

listening_challenge.question: Does Anna want a window or an aisle seat on the plane?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello again. Well, this is very exciting! Paul, the boss, is sending Anna and Tom on a business trip to France. He wants them to clinch the deal with a company interested in buying their Imperial Lemons. But has Tom got more than business on his mind?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Really? What… me and Anna… to France?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes but make sure you get that contract signed. We need the business.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, yeah, of course. Are we staying overnight?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: There's no money for that – just get there and come straight back. Oh and could you bring back those nice French biscuits that have in the duty-free shop?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Sure. So, Anna, we're off on holiday together are we?!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No! But I've got to book the flights online, can you help me please?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: It's not my thing. I'm sure Denise will help. I need to go and pack for this trip.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Yes Marge… in the cupboard… envelopes apparently… Tom and Anna… oh here she is… got to go Marge… bye. Hello Anna, everything OK?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Sort of. I've got to go to France with Tom.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Yes, I know. I thought you'd be pleased to go with Tom, after your time in the stationery cupboard with him!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I was just finding an envelope Denise. Anyway, I'm worried about booking the flights online. I usually book flights at a travel agent's.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: It's company policy now, we have to do everything online – even my food shopping – but don’t tell Paul.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh right. So where shall I begin?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Pull up a chair Anna and we'll log on. Right let's start with the British Airlines website. There. London to Marseille. What is the outbound date?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Going out tomorrow, back tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Business class or Economy class? I think we'll say Economy.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: That's cheaper I guess. What's this mean? Flexible or fixed?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: A flexible ticket means you can change your flight but a fixed one means you can't – and that's cheaper so we'll choose that one. I'll book you on the 8am flight from Heathrow and flying home at 6pm. I just need to type in your full names now and select your seats. Window or aisle?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'll what?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: No Anna. A seat by the aisle or by the window?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, an aisle seat please, Denise.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Good. What's your frequent flyer number?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh I don't have one of those.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What's that? Frequent flyer number? Here I've got a gold status card, can you stick my number in?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Gold status! Where did you get that?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh, I've flown loads of times for business. I've done deals all around the world.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: He means he's been on lots of jollies – free trips paid for by the company – and all he's come home with is a sun tan!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Hmm, really. Right I just need to pay now… using the company account of course.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Cool. Now, what do you think of my sunglasses?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Lovely Tom. Denise has booked you a window seat OK?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: No! Sorry I can't sit by the window… I’m… errr…

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Yes Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Well, I mean, it's only polite that the lady sits by the window.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Really?!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: What's Tom like?! Hopefully he'll prove a useful business partner for Anna on the trip to France. Here's a reminder of some of the questions you may be asked when booking a flight…

transcript.speaker: What's the outbound and return date?
transcript.text:
Do you want to fly business or economy?
Do you want a fixed or flexible ticket?
Would you like a window or aisle seat?
Have you got a frequent flyer number?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: There you go you two, your e-ticket. Now don't forget your passports.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Thanks Denise. Hey Anna, I'm so pleased that we're on this trip together. It'll be nice to spend some time with you.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes and to do some business and really show Paul we are his best employees.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh yeah, of course… I just wondered…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Is there any chance I could sit in the aisle seat?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: I've got a feeling Anna's in for a bumpy ride. Find out how their trip goes next time on English at Work. See ya!
